course_description:
An intermediate course in the ancient Latin language, following on from LATN1110. The course teaches further Latin grammar and gives an introduction to the reading of several Latin authors. NOTE: Instruction by small group teaching.

LATN2120 continues the study of the grammar and syntax of Classical Latin. The course places emphasis on learning through reading.ﾠIt is designed for students who have successfully completed LATN1110 or an equivalent course.ﾠThere are 4 hours instruction per week and regular attendance is expected.

Although classes are recorded, delayed viewing has not been activated for this course because it has an in-class, in person, mid-semester exam, and person attendance becomes more important as the complexity of the grammar increases. If you have a genuine timetable clash but can attend the mid-semester exam, please contact Dr McWilliam to discuss. We can enrol you in the course manually. Microsoft Teams will also be used to facilitate communication and discussion
Classes are scheduled for Wednesday 10am-12pm
AND
Friday 12-2pm in Building 67 Room 348. Please confirm class venues before your first class.
Courses are taught in Blended Mode rather than in lecture/tutorial format, so in each 2 hour block, students will do different combinations of grammar and interactive exercises, reading and parsing to reinforce weekly and cumulative grammar and vocabulary.

course_aims:
In second semester Latin, students will read the concluding section of Plautus' Amphitruo and a selection of Cicero's prosecution speeches against Verres, the former governor of the Roman province of Sicily.

By the end of the semester you should be able to:

learning_outcomes.description: demonstrate In-depth Knowledge of most of the forms, grammar and syntax of the Latin language
demonstrate Effective Communication Skills through completion of the written assignments and through oral translation in class
demonstrate Independence and Critical Judgement in interpreting and translating the graded reading passage
demonstrate Ethical and Social Understanding of the social and cultural values of the Roman world as expressed through its language and literature

assessment_details.task_description: PART 1: ASSIGNMENTS Copies of all Assignments, and their due dates, are on the Blackboard Site for LATN2120. REQUIREMENTS : There are five (5) Assignments in total, designed to increase your skills in translation into English and/or Latin, comprehension, vocab recognition, parsing, grammar and syntax analysis. All five (5) Assignments must be completed (with genuine attempts for ALL questions as instructed) in order to obtain a passing grade for the course Uploading a document without answer(s) does not constitute a genuine submission. Each Assignment is worth 20%. Your final mark will be calculated from the sum of these five assignments divided by 5. Assignments must be submitted typed and in word format via Blackboard by the due time and date. Academic Misconduct: AI, Machine Translation and Referencing Unacknowledged use of Machine Translation and/or AI to complete assessment or unapproved learning tasks may be referred for academic misconduct. If you use AI or Machine Translation to complete assignments, you must both acknowledge this use and explain how and why AI and/or Machine Translation was used. Use of Machine Translation and/or AI to complete assessment tasks while language learning skills are still being developed is likely to result in students failing to meet core learning outcomes for the course. Students relying on Machine Translation and AI to complete assessment are also more likely to fail in-person and other assessment tasks. Part 2: Select Option A or B: These assessment items are designed to help you to acquire vocabulary and to master declension and conjugation patterns in particular Option A uqlatin Extend QUIZZES 15% EITHER 972 or more uqlatin quizzes (located on UQ Extend) completed throughout semester or 2 timed Blackboard quizzes held in conjunction with the mid-semester and final exam uqlatin quizzes: There are 324 quizzes in total. Students must complete 3 genuine attempts at all the following types of quizzes on uqlatin Extend, with their overall number of quizzes attempted equalling 972: noun declensions adjective/pronoun declension verb conjugation word matching/vocab translation translation/identification of prepositions and idiomatic constructions If you elect to take this option, you must start your quiz practice in Week 1, or you will not reach the required number of quizzes by the end of semester. Proper attempts must be made for each question (e.g. a genuine answer must be entered for every question). However, students are not required to get all answers correct to receive the full 15%. The purpose of this assessment task is to make learning vocab meaning, conjugation & declension patterns etc part of your automatic recall/memory. STUDENTS WHO DO NOT TAKE UP THIS OPTION MUST COMPLETE OPTION B: BLACKBOARD TIMED QUIZZES Two (2) timed Blackboard Quizzes held in conjunction with the mid-semester and final exams Each quiz is 10 mins long, and only one attempt is permitted for each quiz. The mark for each quiz will be added together and divided by 2 to calculate the final mark out of 15. Quizzes will cover: noun declensions adjective/pronoun declensions noun/adjective/pronoun/participle matching verb conjugations person and number, verb principal parts, mood tense and voice vocab meaning translation of short phrases Please prepare for these tests by completing some of the UQ Extend quizzes, Blackboard In Class Tests, revising by handwriting, with flashcards, learning vocabulary etc. Details of both assessment tasks are available on Blackboard Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Skill Building: Class Participation and Practice
assessment_details.task_description: Students are required to translate set texts assigned before class, as listed by Section in the Course Profile and on Blackboard. These texts will be re translated and discussed in class in conjunction with points of grammar, syntax, literary style, and where relevant, historical and/or cultural context. A selection will also be re-examined in the mid-semester and final exam. Students should translate the set lines of text before each class. Students will complete worksheets in class. Questions will be based on points of grammar, vocab, and questions based on the set texts prepared for each week and retranslated in class. Points of grammar, syntax, and vocabulary acquisition will also be reinforced though class exercises which are designed to provide immediate feedback, focus on points of grammar and syntax, literary technique, and relevant historical and/or cultural contexts. Students are encouraged to use the class time to ask questions encountered during preparation or that arise in class during translation, discussion, or during the completion of class exercises. Students are encouraged to use the specific Learning Materials that have been developed for this course, which will be explained in Week 1 of the course. Although AI and Machine translation can be used for this task, at beginner level it does not help students to master the skills needed, and in some cases may be misleading and potentially more time-consuming. Nor will foundational skills be mastered by regularly writing down the translations from Blackboard and reading them out without attempting to translate and understand the Latin texts yourself. Use of Machine Translation and/or AI to complete assessment tasks while language learning skills are still being developed is likely to result in students failing to meet core learning outcomes for the course. Students relying on Machine Translation and AI to complete assessment are also more likely to fail in-person assessment tasks. Marking criteria and/or marking rubrics are available in the ‘Assessment’ folder in Blackboard for this course. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Students are required to be in class to translate texts and complete worksheets: written work cannot be submitted in lieu of in-person attendance. While these will not be assigned an individual mark as this exercise is about providing feedback through discussion, they form part of your overall participation mark. In person class participation is demonstrated through active participation in all components of the class: demonstration of prepared translations of set texts for weekly classes on Wednesday and Friday, in-class translation and discussion of set lines of the prepared texts, active engagement in discussions directed by the lecturer and in response to peer questions/discussion, and participation in other class learning activities such as class exercises. Students should aim to participate in minimum of 85% of classes. Please keep in contact with the course coordinator if you are having difficulty.
Deferral or extension
